production.note: US model years 2020 to 2023. First: "The 2020 718 Cayman GT4 and 718 Spyder are available to order now and are expected to reach U.S. dealers in spring 2020." Last: Kelley Blue Book lists the 2023 718 Spyder (414 hp, kbb-2023-718-spyder); for 2024 it lists only the Spyder RS, "lighter, more powerful and considerably more expensive than the non-RS Spyder it replaces" (kbb-2024-718-spyder). End year rests on KBB (a database).

body.note: Two-seat open car with "a manually-operated lightweight fabric top"; sold under its own name with no fixed-roof version.

configuration.note: Spec sheet: "Six-cylinder naturally aspirated boxer engine"

aspiration.note: Spec sheet: "Six-cylinder naturally aspirated boxer engine"

fuel.note: Gasoline flat-six; inferred from the spec sheet's description.

transmission.note: Spec sheet (2020): "6-speed manual transmission with dual-mass flywheel". Porsche, 2021: the 4.0-liter 718 models "have been available to order with the optional seven-speed Porsche dual-clutch transmission (PDK) since June in the U.S."; the manual stayed standard. DCT is Porsche PDK.

powerHp.note: Quote: "Max. power output at engine speed: 414 hp / 7,600 rpm". The press release agrees: "a new 4.0-liter naturally-aspirated flat-six engine developing 414 horsepower" (pcna-2020-718-spyder-gt4). KBB still lists 414 hp for 2023.

weightLb.note: 2020 car with the standard 6-speed manual, standard equipment. Quote: "Curb weight: 3,206 lbs." (718 Spyder column; the 718 Cayman GT4 column reads "3,199 lbs."). Confirmed on a second reading of the sheet.
